questions.q: In the number 5.7, which digit is in the tenths place?
questions.a: The digit 7 is in the tenths place. If a student answers "5," they are confusing the whole number place value with the fractional place value.

questions.q: Explain why 0.5 is the same as the fraction 5/10.
questions.a: 0.5 means 5 tenths, which is written as the fraction 5/10. A student who says "they are not the same" likely doesn't understand that the decimal point denotes a base-10 fractional part.

questions.q: Convert the fraction 24/100 into a decimal.
questions.a: The answer is 0.24. This is found by moving the decimal point two places to the left for a denominator of 100. If a student writes 2.4, they are likely miscounting the number of decimal places needed.

questions.q: Compare 0.3 and 0.03. Which is larger and why?
questions.a: 0.3 is larger because it represents 3 tenths (30/100), whereas 0.03 represents only 3 hundredths (3/100). A student who thinks 0.03 is larger is likely ignoring the place value and just looking at the number of zeros.

questions.q: If you have 8 rupees and 50 paise, how would you write this as a decimal in terms of rupees?
questions.a: It is 8.50 rupees because 50 paise is 50/100 of a rupee. A student who writes 8.05 is failing to recognize that 50 paise is 5 tenths or 50 hundredths of a rupee.

questions.q: Write your own decimal number that is greater than 0.1 but less than 0.2.
questions.a: Any number like 0.11, 0.15, or 0.19 is correct. A student who struggles to provide an answer does not understand that there are many values between tenths.
